OVERVIEW
Rafael Holdings, Inc. (“Rafael Holdings”, “Rafael”, “we” or the “Company”) is a biotechnology company that develops pharmaceuticals and holds interests in clinical and early-stage companies that develop pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Our lead candidate is Trappsol® Cyclo™ (remibetadex), an investigational therapy for the potential treatment of Niemann-Pick Disease Type C (“NPC”), a rare, fatal and progressive genetic disorder. We have completed the pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of Trappsol® Cyclo™ and on October 28, 2026 submitted a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. We also hold: (i) a majority equity interest in LipoMedix Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (“LipoMedix”), a clinical stage pharmaceutical company; (ii) Barer Institute Inc. (“Barer”), a wholly-owned subsidiary holding equity interests in early stage cancer assets; (iii) a majority equity, and debt, interest in Cornerstone Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (“Cornerstone”), formerly known as Rafael Pharmaceuticals Inc., a cancer metabolism-based therapeutics company; (iv) a majority equity interest in Rafael Medical Devices, LLC (“Rafael Medical Devices”), an orthopedic-focused medical device company developing instruments to advance minimally invasive surgeries; and (v) a majority equity interest in Day Three Labs, Inc. (“Day Three”), which empowers third-party manufacturers to bring to market better, cleaner, more precise and predictable versions of their product by utilizing Day Three’s technology and which holds equity and debt interests in two industry related companies . Our primary focus is to obtain FDA approval of Trappsol® Cyclo™, for which we submitted a New Drug Application on October 28, 2026 following the recent completion of Cyclo’s pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial, and, if approved, to bring that product to market. W e also evaluate opportunities to expand our investment portfolio through strategic investments, including in therapeutics, that address high unmet medical needs. We continuously evaluate our other holdings to ensure the future focus of our resources is on core assets and specifically the Trappsol® Cyclo™ clinical development and commercialization efforts.
Historically, we owned real estate assets. As of July 31, 2026, we hold a portion of a commercial building in Jerusalem, Israel as our sole remaining real estate asset.
On March 25, 2025, we consummated the Merger (as defined below) with Cyclo whereby Cyclo became a wholly-owned subsidiary. In May 2023, we first invested in Cyclo, a clinical-stage biotechnology company that develops cyclodextrin-based products for the potential treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. Cyclo’s lead drug candidate is Trappsol® Cyclo™ (hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin, IV), a treatment for NPC. NPC is a rare and fatal autosomal recessive genetic disease resulting in disrupted cholesterol metabolism that impacts the brain, lungs, liver, spleen, and other organs. In January 2017, FDA granted Fast Track designation to Trappsol® Cyclo™ for the treatment of NPC. Initial patient enrollment in the U.S. Phase I study commenced in September 2017 and, in May 2020, Cyclo announced Top Line data indicating Trappsol® Cyclo™ was well tolerated in this study. Cyclo has completed its pivotal Phase 3 Clinical Trial evaluating Trappsol ® Cyclo™ in Pediatric and Adult Patients with Niemann-Pick Disease, Type C and announced topline data from the study on September 30, 2026. The study did not meet its primary endpoint in the overall population; a prespecified analysis in patients receiving background miglustat and/or leucine therapy demonstrated a statistically significant treatment benefit. On October 28, 2026, Cyclo submitted a New Drug Application (“NDA”) to FDA seeking approval of Trappsol® Cyclo™ for the treatment of the neurovisceral manifestations of NPC in adult and pediatric patients from birth. Within 60 days of receipt, the FDA will determine whether the application is complete and acceptable for filing and, if accepted, whether Priority Review will be granted. If the application is accepted, the FDA will assign a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date. The NDA includes a request for a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. The United States Adopted Names (“USAN”) Council has assigned the nonproprietary name “remibetadex” to Trappsol® Cyclo™. In addition, on April 16, 2026, Cyclo entered into an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-bearing Patent License Agreement with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (“MIT”) for certain patent rights relating to small molecules to improve myelination in Alzheimer’s disease and APOE4 carriers, under which Cyclo may develop and commercialize products containing hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin for Alzheimer’s disease.
LipoMedix is a clinical stage Israeli company based in Israel that is focused on the development of a product candidate, Promitil, that holds the potential to be a therapy for cancer based on liposome delivery. As of July 31, 2026, our ownership interest in LipoMedix was approximately 95%. As needed, we provide debt or equity funding to LipoMedix to support its development and clinical efforts. LipoMedix has recently initiated an IST (investigator sponsored study) specifically an open-label, Phase II Single-Arm Trial of PROMITIL Combined with Radiotherapy in patients with Cisplatin-Ineligible Head and Neck Cancer. LipoMedix is also currently exploring strategic options for its lead candidate, including potential licensing opportunities, collaborations with industry partners, and investigator-initiated studies.
In 2019, we established Barer, originally as a preclinical cancer metabolism research operation, to focus on developing a pipeline of novel therapeutic compounds, including compounds designed to regulate cancer metabolism with potentially broader application in other indications beyond cancer. Barer was comprised of scientists and academic advisors that are experts in cancer metabolism, chemistry, and drug development. In addition to its own internal discovery efforts, Barer pursued collaborative research agreements and in-licensing opportunities with leading scientists from top academic institutions. Barer’s majority owned subsidiary, Farber Partners, LLC (“Farber”), was formed around one such agreement with Princeton University’s Office of Technology Licensing (“Princeton”) for technology from the laboratory of Dr. Joshua Rabinowitz, in the Department of Chemistry, Princeton University, for an exclusive worldwide license to its SHMT (serine hydroxymethyltransferase) inhibitor program. In November 2022, we resolved to curtail its early-stage development efforts, including pre-clinical research at Barer and have, since that date, ceased almost all of such activity. Since then, we have sought partners for Farber programs and have entered into a license agreement for one of its technologies that is in the pre-clinical research stage with the Ludwig Institute of Cancer Research and have transferred majority ownership of another one of its technologies, SHMT, to a new company, Forme Therapeutics, that is being managed by Dr. Joshua Rabinowitz with the goal of developing SHMT while seeking out external investment and partnerships. Going forward, we expect that Barer will primarily operate as an entity holding interest in these two cancer-focused opportunities.
On March 13, 2024, Cornerstone consummated a restructuring of its outstanding debt and equity interests (the “Cornerstone Restructuring”). As a result of the Cornerstone Restructuring, Rafael became a 67% owner of the issued and outstanding common stock of Cornerstone (the “Cornerstone Acquisition”), and Cornerstone became a consolidated subsidiary of Rafael. See Note 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information on the Cornerstone Restructuring, Cornerstone Acquisition, and RP Finance Consolidation. We are currently reviewing Cornerstone’s current efforts, prospects and available resources to determine the optimal operational direction.
In May 2021, we formed Rafael Medical Devices, an orthopedic-focused medical device company developing instruments to advance minimally invasive surgeries. In August 2023, Rafael Medical Devices sold an aggregate 31.6% equity interest to third parties for $925,000. In February 2025, we invested approximately $582,000 in cash, and Rafael Medical Devices raised approximately $44,000 from third parties in exchange for Rafael Medical Devices’ Class A Units. In July 2026, we converted the balance of an intercompany promissory note plus accrued interest, totaling $2,087,086, in exchange for Rafael Medical Devices’ Class A Units. As a result, we currently hold an 83% equity interest in Rafael Medical Devices. RISK FACTORS
Our business, operating results or financial condition could be materially adversely affected by any of the following risks associated with any one of our businesses, as well as the other risks highlighted elsewhere in this document. The trading price of our common stock could decline due to any of these risks. Note that references to “our”, “us”, “we”, “the Company”, etc. used in each risk factor below refers to the business about which such risk factor is provided.
Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Capital Needs
Substantial doubt exists regarding our ability to continue as a going concern, and we will require additional financing to fund our operations.
We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company with no approved products and no revenue from product sales. We have incurred recurring losses and expect to continue to incur significant expenses, for a period of at least 12 months from the date of issuance, to support FDA’s review of our New Drug Application for Trappsol ® Cyclo ™ (remibetadex) , submitted on October 28, 2026, and, if approved, to commercialize the product. As a result, management has concluded that substantial doubt exists regarding our ability to continue as a going concern.
Our ability to continue operations depends on our ability to raise additional capital through equity financings, debt financings, strategic collaborations, or other sources. While we are actively pursuing additional financing, there can be no assurance that such funding will be available on acceptable terms, or at all. If we are unable to obtain sufficient capital, we may be required to delay, reduce, or discontinue our clinical development programs or other operations, which could materially adversely affect our business and the value of our common stock.
Our limited operating history makes it difficult to evaluate our business and prospects and may increase your investment risk.
We have only a limited operating history upon which our business and prospects can be evaluated. We expect to encounter risks and difficulties frequently encountered by early-stage companies in the industries in which we operate.
We have not yet demonstrated our ability to successfully complete any large-scale, pivotal clinical trials, obtain regulatory approvals, manufacture any medicine on a commercial scale, or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales and marketing activities necessary for successful commercialization of any product that might receive regulatory approval. Typically, it takes about ten to fifteen years to develop one new medicine from the time it is discovered to when it is available for treating patients. Consequently, any predictions made about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a longer operating history.
In addition, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown factors and risks frequently experienced by clinical stage biopharmaceutical companies in rapidly evolving fields. We will also need to transition from a company with a research focus to a company capable of supporting commercial activities should any regulatory approval be secured, if any. If we do not adequately address these risks and difficulties or successfully make such a transition, our business will suffer, our future revenue potential may be impacted, and our ability to pursue our growth strategy and attain profitability could be compromised.
We hold cash, cash equivalents, convertible notes receivable and investments that are subject to various market risks.
As of July 31, 2026, we held approximately $22.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, $2.0 million in convertible notes receivable classified as available for sale and $0.8 million in investments. Our passive interests in other entities are not currently liquid, and we cannot assure that we will be able to liquidate them when we desire, or ever. As a result of these different market risks, our holdings of cash, cash equivalents, and investments could be materially and adversely affected.
We may not be able to consummate any investment, business combination or other transaction.
While we seek corporate development opportunities, we may not be able to find any suitable target businesses and consummate an investment, business combination or other transaction. Our ability to complete any such transactions may be negatively impacted by general market conditions, volatility in the debt and equity markets, decreased market liquidity, and third-party financing being unavailable on terms acceptable to us or at all.
Risks Related to our Pharmaceuticals Business
Our future success will likely depend on our ability to obtain regulatory approval and successfully commercialize Trappsol ® Cyclo™ (remibetadex). If we are unable to do so, or we experience significant delays in doing so, our business will be materially harmed.
We have invested a significant amount of capital in Cyclo and the development and clinical activity for Trappsol® Cyclo™. Our dependence on the success of Trappsol® Cyclo™ and the possible need for additional capital has increased following completion of the Phase 3 trial for Trappsol ® Cyclo™ and the submission of our NDA on October 28, 2026. Initial top-line data were reported on September 30, 2026 from this pivotal 96-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study (CTD-TCNPC-301) evaluating Trappsol® Cyclo™ (hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin, IV) in 94 patients diagnosed with Niemann-Pick Disease Type C (NPC). Data from the 94-patient trial, with patients ranging in age from 3 to 70 years, indicated that Trappsol® Cyclo™ (2000 mg/kg administered intravenously every two weeks) was well-tolerated and indicated a directionally favorable treatment effect. The complete dataset has been submitted to FDA as part of the NDA and remains subject to FDA review. The Phase 3 study did not meet the primary endpoint in the overall population; a prespecified analysis in patients receiving background miglustat and/or leucine therapy demonstrated a statistically significant and, subject to FDA review of the complete data set, a potential clinically meaningful treatment benefit.
Primary endpoint: Trappsol® Cyclo™ demonstrated a directionally favorable treatment effect compared with placebo, indicating slowing of disease progression by 64% on change in 4DNPCSS at Week 96 (LS mean change from baseline of 0.46 vs 1.28 points; difference −0.81 points [95% CI −2.04, 0.41]; p=0.19); however, the result did not achieve statistical significance.
Prespecified analysis: Among patients receiving background miglustat and/or leucine therapy (n=78), Trappsol® Cyclo™ showed slowing of disease progression of 71% compared with placebo at Week 96 (LS mean change from baseline of 0.46 vs 1.57 points; difference −1.11 points [95% CI −2.19, −0.02]; p=0.046).
